questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.topic: Greatest common divisor of two numbers
questions.learningObjective: explain why a greatest common divisor divides both numbers exactly
questions.stem: Why must the greatest common divisor of two whole numbers divide each of them exactly, with no remainder? Give the explanation.

answer.exemplar: A greatest common divisor is defined as the largest number that divides both whole numbers with no remainder left over, so if it left a remainder it would not be a common divisor at all. The definition also rules out any larger number, which is what makes it the greatest one and not merely a common divisor.

questions.explanation: The definition of a common divisor requires an exact division, so a remainder would disqualify the number at once. The word greatest then adds that no larger number divides both exactly.
questions.hint: Recall the two words in the term itself.

questions.stem: The translator must explain why the least common multiple of two numbers is called the least when many common multiples exist. Give the explanation.

answer.exemplar: Every multiple of 14 is also a multiple of 7, so there are infinitely many shared values, and the term least picks out the smallest of them. questions.stem: The prime factor method for the least common multiple takes the larger exponent of each prime. A translator must explain why that rule works. Give the explanation.

answer.exemplar: A common multiple has to contain, for every prime, at least as many copies as the number with the greater power of that prime, otherwise one of the two numbers would not divide it.
